newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM says mine construction continues.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM says mine construction continues.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday that construction of its Ernest Henry copper-gold mine near Cloncurry in north Queensland was continuing while it closely monitored the outcome of a Federal Court application by an Aboriginal group to halt a power link to the giant project.
"The construction of the mine will continue on schedule but a substantial power supply is required for production," MIM public affairs manager Collin Myers told Reuters.

The North Queensland Electricity Board (NQEB), which is building the power line between the mine site and Mount Isa, said it had agreed not to go on land subject to native Title claims, until the matter is resolved.

The interruption to Ernest Henry's power link plans follows an application by the Kalkadoon Dancers' Association to the Brisbane Federal Court on Monday for an injunction preventing the electricity commission from continuing construction.
The court will had down a decision on Friday.
"NQEB is progressing on the project but have agreed not to go on land subject to native title until the matter is resolved," an NQEB spokesman told Reuters.

The power line construction which started from the mine site several weeks ago, has progressed about 40 km towards Cloncurry and has about 100 km of work ahead before being connected to MIM's Mica Creek power station at Mount Isa by July next year, the NQEB spokesman said.
MIM's Myers said a substantial power supply was required for production at Ernest Henry, which is due for a start-up in the second half of 1997.
"From our point of view, the provision of power to Ernest Henry is important and we'll be monitoring the situation closely," Myers said.
MIM holds 51 percent of the project and manages it.
Savage Resources Ltd holds the balance.
The mine is scheduled to produce at an annual rate of 95,000 tonnes of copper and 120,000 ounces of gold.
The concentrate will be sent by truck to Mount Isa for processing at MIM's copper smelter.
